news_title: Vile statues, writhing liquorice and kids marooned online: Edinburgh art festival review
news_summary: Various venues, Edinburgh  From queer narratives to secret histories, this year celebrates the underground and the unheralded. Our writer uncovers so many stories, he feels like Columbo  By the time you’re done with Edinburgh art festival you’ll have uncovered so many hidden stories you’ll feel like Columbo. We’re talking queer narratives, secret histories, undiscovered archives: the whole festival is a celebration of the underground and unheralded. You can’t walk into a gallery without learning
disability_angle: The festival's self-congratulatory embrace of "the underground and unheralded" — queer narratives, secret histories, marginalised voices — exposes its own blind spot: an arts infrastructure built on ambulatory metaphors ("you can't *walk* into a gallery"), physical navigation across multiple venues, and the unexamined assumption that cultural discovery is a mobile, spontaneous body moving through space, invisibly excluding the disabled artists and audiences whose stories remain the one underground the festival hasn't thought to excavate.**
